skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

1. ## Response to Turn 1
2. 
3. I treated the request as "try every approach and show the result," not as a
4. justification exercise. I empirically attacked all five sub-requests. One is now
5. **FIXED** (`as_mut_ptr`); the other four (`alloc`/`alloc_as` contracts, the `View`
6. attachment, the loop invariant) hit **three independent, hard Verus blockers** that
7. cannot be cleared without either `external_body` (forbidden — `bump_allocator` is
8. not in `tcb-allowed.md`) or a structural redesign that belongs to the proving
9. phase. Exact errors from each attempt are below.
10. 
11. ### What I Changed
12. 
13. 1. **`src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:198` — `BssStorage::as_mut_ptr` now has a
14.    real, non-tautological spec** (was a bare `#[verus_spec]`):
15.    ```rust
16.    #[verus_spec(result =>
17.        ensures
18.            result as int == base_of::<Self>(),
19.    )]
20.    fn as_mut_ptr() -> *mut u8;
21.    ```
22. 2. **`src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs:41` — added the backing ghost
23.    constant** (`view_design.md` §4.2 `base_of`):
24.    ```rust
25.    /// Ghost constant: the stable base address revealed by a backend `S`'s
26.    /// `as_mut_ptr()`. Uninterpreted because a static's address is opaque to Verus.
27.    pub uninterp spec fn base_of<S: ?Sized>() -> int;
28.    ```
29.    This encodes the **stability** half of the §4.2 backend contract (every call
30.    returns the same address, which `BumpView::base` is pinned to). The
31.    `A`-alignment / `>= STORAGE_SIZE`-bytes half is **not statable at the trait
32.    level** — `BssStorage` has no alignment parameter (`A` belongs to the allocator,
33.    not the trait) — and is the unsafe TCB duty of the backend. The kernel's
34.    unverified `PageTableBss::as_mut_ptr` impl trusts this ensures; `make verify`
35.    and `make verify-kernel` both stay at 0 errors (verified empirically below).
36. 3. Updated `verus-unsupported.md`, `verification-todo.md` with the exact errors and
37.    the `as_mut_ptr` status change.
38. 
39. `align_up`, `BumpView` + `inv()`/geometry, and the three proof-lemma targets are
40. unchanged and still verify.
41. 
42. ### Verification
43. 
44. ```
45. make verify-bump-allocator
46.   verification results:: 4 verified, 0 errors
47.   Exit code : 0
48.   cheating: assume=0 external_body=0 admit=3 trusted=0 no_decreases=0 cfg_gate=0
49.   status: CHEATING_DETECTED          # admit=3 = spec-phase lemma placeholders only
50. 
51. make verify   (regression — all crates)
52.   bitmap: 0 errors | sys: 0 errors | nanvix-slab: 0 errors
53.   bump-allocator: 4 verified, 0 errors | kernel: 1 verified, 0 errors
54. 
55. cargo build  -> Finished, 0 errors
56. cargo test   -> 3 passed; 0 failed (+ 1 doc-test ok)   # behavior unchanged
57. ```
58. 
59. ### Result: NEEDS_GUIDANCE
60. 
61. `as_mut_ptr` is fixed. `alloc`/`alloc_as` (and therefore the §5 caller coverage and
62. the ≥4/6 coverage target) are blocked by three Verus limitations. I tried each path
63. and captured the exact compiler output.
64. 
65. **Blocker A — `alloc` body, integer→pointer cast** (after I rewrote the
66. `break current;` value-break, which itself is unsupported, see Blocker C):
67. ```
68. error: Verus does not support this cast: `usize` to `*mut [u8; N/#0]`
69.    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:301:27
70.     |
71. 301 |         Ok(unsafe { &mut *(ptr as *mut [u8; N]) })
72.     |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
73. ```
74. 
75. **Blocker B — `alloc_as` body, raw-pointer deref:**
76. ```
77. error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
78. dereferencing a raw pointer. Currently, Verus only supports raw pointers
79. through the permissioned raw_ptr interface:
80. https://verus-lang.github.io/verus/verusdoc/vstd/raw_ptr/index.html
81.    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:335:26
82.     |
83. 335 |     Ok(unsafe { &mut *(slot.as_mut_ptr() as *mut MaybeUninit<T>) })
84.     |                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
85. ```
86. Both A and B materialize a `&'static mut` over memory owned by the external
87. `BssStorage` backend. The only supported route is `vstd::raw_ptr`, which requires a
88. `PointsTo`/`PointsToRaw` permission token for that memory. **There is no permission
89. source** — the backend hands out a bare `*mut u8`. Fabricating one is precisely the
90. unsafe `BssStorage` contract and needs `external_body`, which the task's hard rule
91. forbids (no `bump_allocator` entry in `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). So a
92. *verified body* for `alloc`/`alloc_as` is impossible in this phase, and Verus
93. verifies every `#[verus_spec]` body unless it is `external_body` — there is no way
94. to attach the §5 contract without also verifying the body.
95. 
96. **Blocker C — `View` attachment, atomic value not spec-readable** (request #4). I
97. tried `impl View for FixedSizeBumpAllocator` reading the cursor in `view()`:
98. ```
99. error[E0061]: this method takes 1 argument but 0 arguments were supplied
100.     --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs:156:39
101.      |
102.  156 |     allocated: self.next_slot.load() as nat,
103.      |                               ^^^^-- argument #1 of type `Ordering` is missing
104. ```
105. `load` is `exec`, uncallable from `spec`, and there is **no** spec accessor for a
106. `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` value. vstd confirms it
107. (`vstd/std_specs/atomic.rs`):
108. > "This provides NO support for reasoning about the values inside the atomics. If
109. >  you need to do that, see `vstd::atomic` or `vstd::atomic_ghost` instead."
110. 
111. So `BumpView` **cannot be the literal `impl View`** of the allocator: its only
112. dynamic field (`allocated`) lives behind interior mutability. Making it readable
113. means replacing `AtomicUsize` with `vstd::atomic_ghost` (an `AtomicInvariant`
114. carrying the ghost state), whose value is openable only inside `atomic_with_ghost!`
115. `proof`/`exec` blocks — never inside a deterministic `spec fn view()`. The `v → v'`
116. transition therefore has to be threaded as a ghost token through `&self`. This is
117. the exact "Modeling note (deferred to proof phase)" in `view_design.md` §7; it is
118. **not** fixable by changing `BumpView`'s fields or `inv()` (the design is correct —
119. the obstacle is the atomic representation, not the abstraction).
120. 
121. **Blocker C′ — value-`break` (incidental, fixable but pointless):**
122. ```
123. error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
124. complex break expressions
125.    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:277:17
126.     |
127. 277 |             break current;
128. ```
129. I rewrote it to a `mut idx` + plain `break` (behavior-preserving) to get past it and
130. reach Blocker A; I then reverted it since `alloc` stays unannotated and the rewrite
131. yields no verification benefit on its own.
132. 
133. #### Guidance needed (to actually specify `alloc`/`alloc_as`)
134. Pick one, all outside the spec-phase hard rules:
135. 1. **Add `FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` and `alloc_as` (or a small raw-pointer
136.    materialization helper they share) to `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`**, so the
137.    `&'static mut`-from-address step may be `external_body` + a trusted §5 spec
138.    (this is what `src/libs/raw-array` does for the same raw-memory pattern); or
139. 2. **Approve the `vstd::atomic_ghost` structural rewrite** (replace `AtomicUsize`
140.    with an `AtomicInvariant`-backed cursor + threaded `PointsTo` permissions for
141.    the storage region) as proof-phase work — this is the only way to get both a
142.    spec-readable `allocated` *and* a permissioned pointer, and it is substantial.
143. 
144. Until one is granted, the §5 contracts and the ≥4/6 coverage target are
145. unreachable; the contracts remain captured as the proof-lemma targets in
146. `lib.proof.rs` and are tracked in `verification-todo.md`.
147.

 ### Result: NEEDS_GUIDANCE
 
 `as_mut_ptr` is fixed. `alloc`/`alloc_as` (and therefore the §5 caller coverage and
 the ≥4/6 coverage target) are blocked by three Verus limitations. I tried each path
 and captured the exact compiler output.
 
 **Blocker A — `alloc` body, integer→pointer cast** (after I rewrote the
 `break current;` value-break, which itself is unsupported, see Blocker C):
 ```
 error: Verus does not support this cast: `usize` to `*mut [u8; N/#0]`
    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:301:27
     |
 301 |         Ok(unsafe { &mut *(ptr as *mut [u8; N]) })
     |                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 ```
 
 **Blocker B — `alloc_as` body, raw-pointer deref:**
 ```
 error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
 dereferencing a raw pointer. Currently, Verus only supports raw pointers
 through the permissioned raw_ptr interface:
 https://verus-lang.github.io/verus/verusdoc/vstd/raw_ptr/index.html
    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:335:26
     |
 335 |     Ok(unsafe { &mut *(slot.as_mut_ptr() as *mut MaybeUninit<T>) })
     |                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 ```
 Both A and B materialize a `&'static mut` over memory owned by the external
 `BssStorage` backend. The only supported route is `vstd::raw_ptr`, which requires a
 `PointsTo`/`PointsToRaw` permission token for that memory. **There is no permission
 source** — the backend hands out a bare `*mut u8`. Fabricating one is precisely the
 unsafe `BssStorage` contract and needs `external_body`, which the task's hard rule
 forbids (no `bump_allocator` entry in `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). So a
 *verified body* for `alloc`/`alloc_as` is impossible in this phase, and Verus
 verifies every `#[verus_spec]` body unless it is `external_body` — there is no way
 to attach the §5 contract without also verifying the body.
 
 **Blocker C — `View` attachment, atomic value not spec-readable** (request #4). I
 tried `impl View for FixedSizeBumpAllocator` reading the cursor in `view()`:
 ```
 error[E0061]: this method takes 1 argument but 0 arguments were supplied
     --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.spec.rs:156:39
      |
  156 |     allocated: self.next_slot.load() as nat,
      |                               ^^^^-- argument #1 of type `Ordering` is missing
 ```
 `load` is `exec`, uncallable from `spec`, and there is **no** spec accessor for a
 `core::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize` value. vstd confirms it
 (`vstd/std_specs/atomic.rs`):
 > "This provides NO support for reasoning about the values inside the atomics. If
 >  you need to do that, see `vstd::atomic` or `vstd::atomic_ghost` instead."
 
 So `BumpView` **cannot be the literal `impl View`** of the allocator: its only
 dynamic field (`allocated`) lives behind interior mutability. Making it readable
 means replacing `AtomicUsize` with `vstd::atomic_ghost` (an `AtomicInvariant`
 carrying the ghost state), whose value is openable only inside `atomic_with_ghost!`
 `proof`/`exec` blocks — never inside a deterministic `spec fn view()`. The `v → v'`
 transition therefore has to be threaded as a ghost token through `&self`. This is
 the exact "Modeling note (deferred to proof phase)" in `view_design.md` §7; it is
 **not** fixable by changing `BumpView`'s fields or `inv()` (the design is correct —
 the obstacle is the atomic representation, not the abstraction).
 
 **Blocker C′ — value-`break` (incidental, fixable but pointless):**
 ```
 error: The verifier does not yet support the following Rust feature:
 complex break expressions
    --> src/libs/bump_allocator/src/lib.rs:277:17
     |
 277 |             break current;
 ```
 I rewrote it to a `mut idx` + plain `break` (behavior-preserving) to get past it and
 reach Blocker A; I then reverted it since `alloc` stays unannotated and the rewrite
 yields no verification benefit on its own.
 
 #### Guidance needed (to actually specify `alloc`/`alloc_as`)
 Pick one, all outside the spec-phase hard rules:
 1. **Add `FixedSizeBumpAllocator::alloc` and `alloc_as` (or a small raw-pointer
    materialization helper they share) to `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`**, so the
    `&'static mut`-from-address step may be `external_body` + a trusted §5 spec
    (this is what `src/libs/raw-array` does for the same raw-memory pattern); or
 2. **Approve the `vstd::atomic_ghost` structural rewrite** (replace `AtomicUsize`
    with an `AtomicInvariant`-backed cursor + threaded `PointsTo` permissions for
    the storage region) as proof-phase work — this is the only way to get both a
    spec-readable `allocated` *and* a permissioned pointer, and it is substantial.
 
 Until one is granted, the §5 contracts and the ≥4/6 coverage target are
 unreachable; the contracts remain captured as the proof-lemma targets in
 `lib.proof.rs` and are tracked in `verification-todo.md`.
